prompt: The illustration shows a single cross-section of contemporary work under algorithmic management: a glowing software supervisor floats above a street and office floor, its body composed of performance scores, shift charts, route maps, star ratings, warning icons, policy pages, and chat bubbles. Gig workers—a courier and a driver—are tracked by phone screens and confronted by automatic routing, ratings, and a deactivation symbol, while an office worker faces a personable AI agent that is simultaneously writing a policy and speaking in reassuring text bubbles. To one side, opaque automated pipelines deliver decisions with no visible reasoning; to the other side, a worker steps toward an accessible human manager at a desk with an open appeals folder, a corrected record, and a readable explanation of the decision. The visual contrast should make the entry’s question immediate: can workers understand, challenge, and override the machine’s judgments, or are they managed by systems they cannot reach?
